items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: across the street from it was Lucille's when she had her first club

ctx.x: Well, what happened to the -- I mean, when it became the Cherry Blossom? Was it a dance hall then, or --

It had become one of those huge night-clubs. And this was on Vine Street, between 18th and 19th, directly across the street from the Booker T. Washington Hotel, which by that time had become the most popular one for musicians, you see. And next door to it -- across the street from it was Lucille's when she had her first club. Before she moved around on 18th Street. And next door to it on the right was a club known as the Kentucky Tavern. And that's where jam sessions would usually start around 2:00 o'clock in the…
